rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while limiting the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to test selectivity around the sole unresolved pair. The ample time margin allows us to prioritize resolving this cluster without lengthening the gradient yet.

Test the upper temperature limit with the gradient unchanged to map selectivity changes in the central cluster. Heating improved the minimum resolution, but the neighboring gaps also shifted, so this run will establish whether further heating helps or creates a new critical pair.

Use a shallower gradient at the best temperature so far to improve the central separation without approaching the co-elution seen at 60 C. The current last-peak time of 6.81 minutes leaves room to lengthen the gradient while targeting elution within 10 minutes.

Combine the shallower gradient’s larger neighboring gaps with an intermediate temperature to separate the remaining critical pair. At 55 C, temperature-driven selectivity may resolve that pair without causing the co-elution observed at 60 C, while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is achieved; now shorten the gradient by one step to seek faster fully resolved elution. Keep temperature and endpoints fixed to test whether both critical gaps remain at or above R = 1.5.

Slightly reduce the gradient slope by lowering phi1 one step, targeting recovery of the marginal R = 1.47 pair. This should provide an intermediate separation between the 12- and 14-minute gradients, potentially retaining full resolution with faster elution than injection 5.

Shift both endpoints upward by 0.05 while preserving injection 7’s gradient slope to test whether stronger initial solvent shortens elution without sacrificing full resolution. Injection 7 remains the fastest fully resolved method tested.

Test a weaker start combined with a shorter, steeper gradient: lowering phi0 may restore the sensitive central gap while the steeper slope accelerates late elution. This explores a faster alternative while retaining injection 7 as the fully resolved benchmark.

Increase phi1 by one grid step to test a slightly steeper, faster gradient from the best fully resolved starting composition. Both critical gaps have little margin, so this probes the speed limit while retaining injection 9 as the benchmark.

Explore the untested low-temperature selectivity regime, where changes in elution order may separate the central cluster without a longer gradient. The scouting run’s time margin makes this a reasonable alternative to the narrowly balanced 55 C methods.

Test a stronger start at 60 C to see whether the central pair moves through its selectivity crossover and separates in reversed order. This explores a substantially faster regime while retaining injection 9 as the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Lower the starting organic fraction to recover early-pair resolution, while steepening the gradient to probe the reversed-order central separation at 60 C. This tests whether the fast regime can be balanced into full resolution.

Shorten the gradient one step to test whether steeper elution improves the reversed-order central pair at 60 C. Monitor its neighboring gap closely, since it has only a small resolution margin; injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Return to 40 C and test a shallower gradient, which may move its critical pair apart rather than toward the crossover seen at 50 C. The high endpoint should keep all compounds eluting, with the last peak expected near the 10-minute scoring boundary.

Test whether cooling to 35 C separates the critical central pair sufficiently to permit a shorter gradient than injection 15. The neighboring gaps will show whether this lower-temperature regime offers a fully resolved alternative.

Test whether cooling the fast gradient from injection 13 restores the central gap without collapsing the other temperature-sensitive separation. This directly probes a faster alternative to the fully resolved 55 C benchmark.

Lower the starting organic fraction to widen the central gap that limited injection 17, while increasing the gradient slope to test improvement of its other unresolved pair. This probes a faster 50 C alternative while preserving injection 9 as the fastest fully resolved method.

Probe whether a steeper gradient at 30 C separates the low-temperature cluster through altered selectivity rather than simply stretching it. This is an exploratory faster regime; injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method.

Return to the successful 55 C region with a slope between injections 6 and 7, targeting full resolution with faster elution than injection 7. The predicted last peak should elute before the gradient ends, so the lower endpoint should not delay it.

Shorten the programmed gradient while preserving injection 9’s starting composition and slope. Because its last peak eluted at 7.60 minutes, before this gradient would finish at the outlet, full resolution should be retained with a lower final organic fraction.

Refine the stronger-start method from injection 8 by reducing its slope to recover the unresolved central gap. This may provide full resolution with a larger minimum-resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Lengthen injection 22’s gradient one step to recover its sole unresolved pair, targeting a fully resolved alternative with more margin in the other critical gap. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes; injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 23 to balance its two critical gaps and seek a larger resolution margin while retaining CRF 1.000. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes; injection 9 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Refine injection 24 with a slightly shallower slope to balance its two critical resolutions, targeting additional separation margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 9 remains the fastest verified fully resolved method, already achieving the maximum CRF.
